ecopedia.summary: A Rabotnik must be a citizen with a home before it will work.
ecopedia.section: A Rabotnik always tries to become a citizen of the settlement its [Rabotnik Logbook] is in. It goes through the settlement's normal [Immigration Policy], so a settlement that doesn't accept new citizens won't accept Rabotniks either. Until it is accepted, the Rabotnik waits, and its Logbook says why.

A Rabotnik rents a home exactly as a player accepts a [Residency] invitation. It tries these in order: 1. The deed the Logbook stands on. 2. Otherwise, the cheapest residence in the settlement that has invited it and that it can afford.
The deed's owner must invite the Rabotnik, either by name or by inviting Everyone or a group that includes it. A Rabotnik never rents a residence whose rent only covers online hours, because a Rabotnik is never online and would live there for free.

A Rabotnik only moves in if it can pay the move-in fee plus 24 hours of rent, by default. Fund it from the Logbook's Home and Money tab.
After that, rent is charged every hour by the normal rent system. If the Rabotnik can't pay, it is evicted like any tenant and stops working until it finds a new home. The Logbook's owner is warned when the Rabotnik has less than 12 hours of rent left.
Once a Rabotnik is working, its wages normally cover its rent. Money you give a Rabotnik is its own and can't be taken back. See [Rabotniks Overview].
Like a player, a Rabotnik's home adds to its [Experience] rate, which affects how fast it levels up its skill. See [Rabotnik Food and Skills].
